ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the sea area in the figure marks the positions of meridians, and labels such as 172.5°, 180°, and 172.5° can be seen at the top. In the middle there is a vertical dashed line indicating the International Date Line near 180°. The range shown in the figure is near the International Date Line, and the ship will cross the International Date Line 10 minutes later. Then reason: the local zone time given in the question is 11:20 on May 17, 2005, and after 10 minutes the time first becomes 11:30. When crossing the International Date Line, if crossing from west to east, the date should be reduced by one day, becoming 11:30 on May 16; if crossing from east to west, the date should be increased by one day, becoming 11:30 on May 18. In both directions it is impossible for it still to be May 17, so the date and zone time that could not appear within the range shown in the figure is 11:30 on May 17.
